title: Pre-Analysis — Stabilised Antenna Drive Retrofit Beyond the Launch Operators

ata.title: Independent Position Determining — Weather Radar Transceiver

abstract: Closed re-analysis of the stabilised antenna drive standard, run on a proposal to make the retrofit a fleet campaign, which was sent back for re-scoping when the training cost turned out to dominate the case.

sections.objective: Assess a proposal to convert the stabilised antenna drive retrofit from a customer option into a fleet campaign, on the argument that a single standard across the fleet is worth more than the sum of the individual business cases.
sections.findings_summary: The proposal was sent back for re-scoping. Three items were confirmed. The decisive one was not technical: the crew description already tells the pilot that knowing which radar standard the aircraft carries matters because the two behave differently in the flare, and moving to one standard removes that burden, but the training cost of re-teaching the approach technique across every operator had not been in the proposal at all. When it was added the campaign case became worse than the sum of the individual cases it was meant to replace. Second, the drive is supplied as a matched set with the antenna and the supplier could not sustain a campaign rate. Third, a third operator was mid-way through the existing bulletin and a campaign would have stranded its remaining kits.
sections.next_steps: Re-scope the proposal with the training cost included and the supplier rate as a constraint. Keep the existing bulletin as the vehicle. Re-approach the question when the third issue of the standard is defined, since a single training event covering both changes would carry a cost that a campaign for this change alone cannot.

similarity_seeds: the cost of teaching one technique across a fleet that flies two standards

tasks.title: Build the campaign case including training
Check supplier rate against a campaign
Check the position of operators mid-bulletin

evidence.similarity_note: The crew description and the modification share no identifier; the connection is the behaviour in the flare region that one describes to a pilot and the other changes in hardware.

expected_findings.rationale: The crew description carries the two-standard distinction explicitly, and removing it is the real benefit of a campaign. The cost of re-teaching the approach technique across every operator had not been counted, and when it was the campaign case failed.
expected_findings.resolution: Proposal sent back for re-scoping with the training cost included.

expected_findings.rationale: A third operator was mid-way through the existing bulletin with kits already ordered. A campaign would have stranded them without any mechanism to tell the operator that it had happened.
expected_findings.resolution: Existing bulletin retained as the vehicle.

expected_findings.rationale: A campaign would have let the pre-modification interface unit be withdrawn from the figure earlier than planned, which was the only documentation benefit identified.
expected_findings.resolution: Recorded; no action taken because the campaign was not approved.

expected_non_findings.reason: Returned by every entity search as the predecessor. Its supersession was already declared and it added nothing to a question about campaign economics.

type_data.conclusion: Campaign proposal rejected and returned for re-scoping. The training cost dominates and had not been counted.
